en: wizard; master (of a skill); Taoist ascetic

examples.en: My dad is a computer wizard.
There is an old tale about meeting a hermit sage in the mountains.

examples.ko: 길 찾기 도사가 우리 반에 있어요.
examples.en: We have a master at finding directions in our class.
I solved the problem as quickly as a master.

examples.ko: 영화에 나오는 도사는 구름을 타고 다녀요.
examples.en: The sage in the movie travels riding on clouds.
He is famous as a gaming wizard.

explain: 원래는 도를 닦은 사람이지만 요즘은 '컴퓨터 도사', '요리 도사'처럼 어떤 일에 아주 능숙한 사람에게 가볍게 써요. 칭찬이지만 친한 사이에서 농담처럼 말할 때가 많아요.
explain_en: Originally it meant a sage who trained in the Way, but today people lightly say 'computer 도사' or 'cooking 도사' for someone very skilled at something. It is praise, but mostly used jokingly between friends.

examples.en: You have to enter a string in this field.
I learned how to count the length of a string.
I saved it as a string, not as a number.
If the string is too long, an error occurs.

examples.ko: 이 함수는 글자를 거꾸로 바꾸는 문자열 처리를 해요.
examples.en: This function does string processing that reverses the characters.

examples.ko: 빈 문자열은 아무 글자도 없는 값이에요.
examples.en: An empty string is a value with no characters at all.

explain: 프로그래밍에서 숫자와 구별해서 글자를 이어 놓은 값을 말할 때 써요. 일상 대화에서는 거의 안 쓰고 '문자열 처리', '문자열 길이'처럼 컴퓨터 이야기에서 나와요.
explain_en: In programming it is used to separate a run of characters from a number. It almost never appears in daily talk; you see it in computer topics like 'string processing' or 'string length'.

examples.en: A police officer helped a lost child.
I met a young police officer at the police box.

examples.ko: 아버지는 삼십 년 전에 순경으로 일을 시작하셨어요.
examples.en: My father started working as a police officer thirty years ago.
Officer, I lost my wallet.
The officer patrols the neighborhood every night.

examples.ko: 시험에 합격해서 꼭 순경이 되고 싶어요.
examples.en: I want to pass the exam and become a police officer.

explain: 경찰 계급 중 가장 낮은 편이라 길에서 만나는 경찰관이 대개 순경이에요. 평소 말할 때는 그냥 '경찰'이나 '경찰관'이라고 많이 하고, 부를 때는 '순경님'이라고 해요.
explain_en: It is the lowest police rank, so the officers you meet on the street are often 순경. In everyday talk people usually just say 경찰 or 경찰관, and you address one as 순경님.

examples.en: My younger sibling swiped one of my snacks.

examples.ko: 누가 내 펜을 슬쩍해 갔나 봐요.
examples.en: Someone seems to have swiped my pen.
I heard he got caught swiping an apple at the market.

examples.ko: 친구 지우개를 슬쩍한 적이 있어서 아직도 미안해요.
examples.en: I once swiped a friend's eraser, and I still feel sorry.
You must not swipe other people's things.
I almost swiped a candy in the store, but I held back.

explain: '훔치다'보다 가볍고 구어적이라 장난처럼 들려요. 그래서 진짜 도둑질을 말할 때는 조심해서 써요. 부사 '슬쩍'은 몰래 살짝 한다는 느낌으로 훨씬 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is lighter and more colloquial than 훔치다 and can sound playful, so be careful using it for real theft. The adverb 슬쩍, meaning quietly and lightly, is much more common.

examples.en: After long treatment, the illness was completely cured.

examples.ko: 이 병은 일찍 발견하면 완치될 수 있어요.
examples.en: If this disease is found early, it can be completely cured.
To be fully cured, you have to keep taking the medicine.
Grandmother was fully cured and left the hospital.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님이 곧 나을 거라고 하시고 완치된 환자도 많다고 했어요.
examples.en: The doctor said I will get better soon and that many patients were fully cured.
You need to rest from exercise until you are fully cured.

explain: '낫다'는 감기 같은 가벼운 병에도 쓰지만 '완치되다'는 오래 치료한 병에 주로 써요. '완치율', '완치 판정'처럼 명사로도 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 낫다 works for light illnesses like a cold, but 완치되다 is mostly for illnesses treated for a long time. It also appears often in nouns like 완치율 (cure rate) and 완치 판정 (declared cured).

examples.ko: 시끄러운 곳에 다녀온 뒤 이명이 생겼어요.
examples.en: After visiting a noisy place, I got ringing in my ears.

examples.ko: 밤에 조용하면 이명이 더 크게 들려요.
examples.en: When it is quiet at night, the ringing sounds louder.

examples.ko: 의사 선생님께 이명 때문에 왔다고 말했어요.
examples.en: I told the doctor I came because of tinnitus.

examples.ko: 이명 증상이 심해서 잠을 잘 못 자요.
examples.en: My tinnitus is bad, so I can't sleep well.
Tinnitus gets worse when I am tired.
My father has had tinnitus for a long time.

explain: 의학 용어라 병원이나 건강 이야기에서 주로 나와요. 친구끼리는 '귀에서 삐 소리가 나요'처럼 풀어서 말할 때가 많아요. '이명이 있다', '이명이 들리다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: It is a medical term, so it mainly appears at the hospital or in health talk. Among friends people often say it in plain words, like 'there is a beeping sound in my ear'. It goes with 이명이 있다 and 이명이 들리다.

examples.ko: 세균 증식을 막으려면 음식을 냉장고에 넣어야 해요.
examples.en: To prevent bacteria from multiplying, you have to put food in the fridge.
The cancer cells are proliferating fast.

examples.ko: 이 약은 바이러스 증식을 늦춰 줘요.
examples.en: This medicine slows the multiplication of viruses.

examples.ko: 잡초 증식 때문에 정원이 엉망이 됐어요.
examples.en: The garden became a mess because the weeds multiplied.
When it is warm and humid, mold multiplies easily.
He is very interested in growing his wealth.

explain: 세포·세균·곰팡이처럼 살아 있는 것이 불어날 때 주로 써요. 재산이 불어날 때도 쓰지만 일상 대화에서는 '늘다', '불다'를 더 많이 해요. '증식하다'보다 '세포 증식'처럼 명사로 자주 나와요.
explain_en: It is mainly for living things like cells, bacteria, and mold multiplying. It can also be used for growing wealth, but in daily talk people say 늘다 or 불다. It appears more often as a noun, like 세포 증식, than as the verb.

examples.en: Bacteria multiply quickly in warm places.
It is dangerous if cancer cells proliferate in the body.
Mold multiplied and the wall turned black.

examples.ko: 이 균은 물속에서도 증식할 수 있어요.
examples.en: This germ can multiply even in water.
I observed the multiplying cells under a microscope.

examples.ko: 바이러스가 증식하기 전에 치료를 시작해야 해요.
examples.en: You have to start treatment before the virus multiplies.

explain: 스스로 번식하듯 수가 늘어나는 느낌이라 세균·세포·식물에 잘 어울려요. 사람이나 물건 수가 늘 때는 '늘다', '늘어나다'를 쓰고 '증식하다'는 잘 안 써요.
explain_en: It has the feel of multiplying on its own, so it suits bacteria, cells, and plants. For numbers of people or things, use 늘다 or 늘어나다 instead of 증식하다.

examples.en: The air is crisp and refreshing as I climb the mountain.
A cool, refreshing breeze brushed past my face.
The sound of the valley stream was clear and refreshing.

examples.ko: 비 온 뒤라서 하늘이 청량해 보여요.
examples.en: The sky looks fresh and clear because it just rained.
I like this song because the voice is clear and fresh.
In summer, crisp, cool drinks are popular.

explain: 시원하고 맑아서 상쾌한 느낌에 써요. 공기·바람·소리·음료 광고에 잘 나오는 글말 느낌의 단어라, 일상 대화에서는 '시원하다', '상쾌하다'를 더 많이 해요. '청량음료'처럼 합성어로도 써요.
explain_en: It describes a cool, clear, refreshing feeling. It has a written tone often seen with air, wind, sound, and drink ads, so daily talk prefers 시원하다 or 상쾌하다. It also appears in compounds like 청량음료 (soft drink).

en: improve; take a turn for the better

examples.en: My health improved after I received treatment.
If the economy improves, jobs will increase.
The patient's condition is improving little by little.

examples.ko: 두 나라의 관계가 호전될 기미가 보여요.
examples.en: There are signs that the relationship between the two countries will improve.
The weather improved, so the plane took off.
The symptoms have not improved yet.

explain: 병세·상황·경기처럼 나쁘던 것이 좋은 쪽으로 바뀔 때 써요. '좋아지다'보다 딱딱해서 뉴스·병원·경제 이야기에 잘 나와요. 반대는 '악화되다'예요.
explain_en: Use it when something bad, like an illness, a situation, or the economy, turns for the better. It is stiffer than 좋아지다 and fits news, hospital, and economy talk. The opposite is 악화되다.

examples.en: This medicine improves the patient's symptoms.

examples.ko: 새 정책이 경제 상황을 호전시킬 거예요.
examples.en: The new policy will improve the economic situation.

examples.ko: 운동은 건강을 호전시키는 데 도움이 돼요.
examples.en: Exercise helps improve your health.
The doctor improved the condition through treatment.
The company held a dinner to improve the mood.

examples.ko: 대화가 두 사람의 관계를 호전시켜 줬어요.
examples.en: The conversation improved the relationship between the two.

explain: '호전되다'는 저절로 좋아지는 것이고 '호전시키다'는 누군가나 무언가가 좋아지게 만드는 것이에요. 주어는 사람이나 약·정책이고 목적어는 상태·상황·건강이에요. 일상 대화보다 보고서나 뉴스에서 써요.
explain_en: 호전되다 is improving on its own, while 호전시키다 is someone or something making it improve. The subject is a person, medicine, or policy, and the object is a condition, situation, or health. It is used in reports and news more than in daily talk.

examples.ko: 환생을 믿는 사람도 있고 안 믿는 사람도 있어요.
examples.en: Some people believe in reincarnation and some do not.

examples.ko: 이 웹소설은 환생 이야기라서 인기가 많아요.
examples.en: This web novel is popular because it is a rebirth story.

examples.ko: 죽은 사람이 다시 태어난다는 환생 이야기를 읽었어요.
examples.en: I read a reincarnation story about a dead person being born again.

examples.ko: 영화에서 주인공은 환생 덕분에 두 번째 삶을 얻어요.
examples.en: In the movie, the hero gets a second life thanks to reincarnation.

examples.ko: 환생이 정말 있을까 하고 가끔 생각해요.
examples.en: I sometimes wonder whether reincarnation really exists.
I like comics that deal with reincarnation.

explain: 불교의 윤회 사상과 이어지는 단어예요. 요즘은 드라마나 웹소설에서 '환생물'처럼 다시 태어나 새 인생을 사는 이야기에 아주 많이 나와요. 고양이나 새로 다시 태어나는 이야기도 흔해요.
explain_en: It connects to the Buddhist idea of the cycle of rebirth. Today it appears a lot in dramas and web novels, in stories like 환생물 where someone is reborn and lives a new life. Stories of being reborn as a cat or a bird are common too.

en: be reincarnated; be reborn; come back to life in a new form

examples.en: The main character is reincarnated as a cat.
I wonder where I will be reborn after I die.
The king was reborn as an ordinary boy.
If I were reborn, I would like to be a bird.
Many writers write stories about reincarnation.

examples.ko: 그는 천 년 뒤에 사람으로 환생했어요.
examples.en: A thousand years later, he was reborn as a person.

explain: '태어나다'는 보통의 탄생이고 '환생하다'는 죽은 존재가 다시 태어난다는 이야기에 써요. '고양이로 환생하다'처럼 새 모습 뒤에 '로'를 붙여요. 현실 대화보다 소설·드라마에서 자주 나와요.
explain_en: 태어나다 is an ordinary birth, while 환생하다 is for a dead being born again. Put 로 after the new form, as in 고양이로 환생하다. It appears more in novels and dramas than in real conversation.

examples.en: That child fought with his parents and ran away from home.
There is an organization that helps teenagers who run away from home.
My younger brother ran away from home, and the whole family went looking for him.

examples.ko: 어릴 때 한 번 가출한 적이 있어요.
examples.en: I ran away from home once when I was little.
The teacher said you must not run away from home.
My friend packed a bag to run away from home.

explain: 단순히 집을 나가는 것은 '집을 나가다'라고 해요. '가출하다'는 말없이 나가서 돌아오지 않는 경우라 뉴스에서 '가출 청소년'처럼 자주 나와요.
explain_en: Simply leaving the house is 집을 나가다. 가출하다 is leaving without a word and not coming back, and it often appears in the news as 가출 청소년 (runaway teens).

en: carry out resolutely; go ahead despite risk

examples.en: The team went ahead with the hike even though it was raining.

examples.ko: 위험을 무릅쓰고 투자를 감행한 회사는 큰 이익을 얻었어요.
examples.en: The company that went ahead with the risky investment made a big profit.
He decided to go ahead with the major surgery.
They say the army might launch an attack.
The rescue team goes out even in a blizzard.

examples.ko: 무리하게 감행하면 성공할 수도 있지만 실패할 수도 있어요.
examples.en: If you push ahead recklessly, you might succeed, but you might also fail.

explain: 위험이나 반대가 있는데도 마음먹고 밀어붙여 할 때 써요. 그냥 '하다'가 아니라 '무릅쓰고 한다'는 느낌이에요. 뉴스에서 '수술을 감행하다', '발사를 감행하다'처럼 써요.
explain_en: Use it when you go ahead with something despite risk or opposition. In the news you see 수술을 감행하다 (go ahead with surgery) and 발사를 감행하다 (go ahead with a launch).

examples.ko: 보석 가게 강탈 사건이 뉴스에 나왔어요.
examples.en: A jewelry store robbery was on the news.
He was caught by the police on suspicion of robbery.

examples.ko: 재산 강탈에 맞서 마을 사람들이 모였어요.
examples.en: The villagers gathered to stand against the seizure of their property.

examples.ko: 역사 시간에 땅 강탈의 아픈 역사를 배웠어요.
examples.en: In history class, I learned the painful history of land seizure.
Robbery is a serious crime, so the punishment is heavy.

examples.ko: 영화에서 보석 강탈 장면이 가장 긴장됐어요.
examples.en: The jewel robbery scene was the most tense part of the movie.

explain: '도둑질'은 몰래 훔치는 것이고 '강탈'은 힘이나 위협으로 억지로 빼앗는 것이에요. 법률·뉴스 단어라 일상 대화에서는 '빼앗다'를 더 많이 해요. 나라나 권리를 빼앗는 일에도 써서 '주권 강탈'처럼 말해요.
explain_en: 도둑질 is stealing secretly, while 강탈 is taking by force or threat. It is a news and legal word; daily talk uses 빼앗다. It also covers taking a country or rights, as in 주권 강탈 (seizure of sovereignty).

examples.en: The team leader read the document and approved it.

examples.ko: 사장님이 결재해 주셔야 일을 시작할 수 있어요.
examples.en: We can start only after the president signs off on it.
The department head reads the report carefully and then approves it.

examples.ko: 제가 먼저 결재하고 나서 부서에 보낼게요.
examples.en: I will approve it first and then send it to the department.
The director decided to approve this matter.
It was an urgent document, so I approved it right away.

explain: 회사에서 윗사람이 서류를 검토하고 승인하는 일에 써요. 소리가 같은 '결제하다'(돈을 내다)와 헷갈리기 쉬워서 글을 쓸 때 조심해야 해요. 서류를 낸 사람은 '결재를 올리다/받다'라고 해요.
explain_en: It is for a superior reviewing and approving a document at work. It sounds the same as 결제하다 (to pay), so be careful when writing. The person who submitted the document says 결재를 올리다 or 결재를 받다.

en: seasoned experience; wisdom from long experience

examples.ko: 사장님은 경륜이 풍부해서 회사를 잘 이끄세요.
examples.en: The president has rich experience and leads the company well.

examples.ko: 오랜 경륜 덕분에 어려운 문제도 해결했어요.
examples.en: Thanks to long experience, we solved even the hard problem.
There is a lot to learn from the teacher's seasoned experience.

examples.ko: 경륜 있는 의사를 만나서 안심이 됐어요.
examples.en: I felt relieved to meet an experienced doctor.

examples.ko: 그분은 일을 오래 하셔서 경륜이 대단해요.
examples.en: He has worked for a long time, so his experience is impressive.

examples.ko: 젊은 직원들은 경륜을 쌓으려고 열심히 일해요.
examples.en: The young employees work hard to build up experience.

explain: 오랜 경험에서 나온 지혜와 안목을 가리켜요. 보통 나이 많은 사람이나 전문가를 높이는 말이라 '경륜이 있다', '경륜이 풍부하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '경험'이나 '연륜'을 더 많이 써요.
explain_en: It points to wisdom and judgment that come from long experience. It usually praises older people or experts, as in 경륜이 있다 or 경륜이 풍부하다. In daily talk 경험 or 연륜 is more common.

examples.en: I decided to donate bone marrow to my younger sibling.

examples.ko: 골수 이식 수술은 몇 시간 걸려요.
examples.en: A bone marrow transplant takes several hours.
The doctor said a bone marrow test is needed.

examples.ko: 소뼈의 골수가 국물에 녹아 진한 맛이 나요.
examples.en: The marrow of the beef bones melts into the broth and gives a rich taste.

examples.ko: 건강한 사람도 골수 기증을 등록할 수 있어요.
examples.en: Healthy people can also register for bone marrow donation.

examples.ko: 저는 이 팀의 골수팬이라서 경기를 한 번도 안 놓쳤어요.
examples.en: I am a die-hard fan of this team, so I have never missed a game.

explain: 건강 뉴스에서는 '골수 이식', '골수 기증'처럼 한 덩어리로 자주 나와요. 비유로는 뼛속까지 깊이 들어갔다는 느낌을 살려 '골수팬'처럼 써요.

phrases.nuance_ko: 아주 오래, 깊이 좋아하는 팬이에요. '열성팬'보다 더 오래된 충성스러운 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fan who has loved something deeply for a long time, with a feel of long-standing loyalty.

explain_en: In health news it shows up as set phrases like 골수 이식 (transplant) and 골수 기증 (donation). Figuratively, it keeps the feel of 'deep to the bone', as in 골수팬.

examples.ko: 이 문제는 우리 학교에만 국한되지 않아요.
examples.en: This problem is not limited to our school.
The story is limited to a single topic.
Participation in the event will be limited to students.

examples.ko: 그 인기는 어린이에게만 국한되는 것이 아니에요.
examples.en: That popularity is not limited to children.

examples.ko: 우리 회사의 고민은 비용에 국한되어 있지 않아요.
examples.en: My company's worries are not confined to cost.
The conversation was limited to work talk, so it was boring.

explain: '~에 국한되다'처럼 범위를 나타내는 '~에'와 같이 써요. '~뿐이다', '~에 한하다'와 비슷하지만 글이나 발표에서 더 자주 나와요. '~에 국한되지 않다'가 특히 많아요.
explain_en: It pairs with 에 to show the range, as in ~에 국한되다. It is close to ~뿐이다 or ~에 한하다, but appears more in writing and presentations. The negative ~에 국한되지 않다 is especially common.

examples.ko: 이번 조사는 서울에 사는 학생으로 국한했어요.
examples.en: This survey was limited to students living in Seoul.

examples.ko: 질문은 오늘 배운 내용으로 국한해 주세요.
examples.en: Please limit your questions to what we learned today.
Don't confine the scope too narrowly.
We decided to limit the presentation to ten minutes.

examples.ko: 연구를 한 가지 문제에 국한한 것이 아쉬워요.
examples.en: It's a pity that the research was confined to one problem.

examples.ko: 우리는 대화를 업무 이야기로 국한할 필요가 없어요.
examples.en: We don't need to limit our conversation to work talk.

explain: '국한되다'는 저절로 범위가 정해지는 것이고 '국한하다'는 사람이 일부러 범위를 정하는 것이에요. '~로 국한하다'처럼 써요. 일상 대화에서는 '~만 하다'로 간단히 말해요.
explain_en: 국한되다 is the range settling on its own, while 국한하다 is a person setting the range on purpose. Use it like ~로 국한하다. In daily talk people simply say ~만 하다.

en: be derived; be deduced; be reached (as a conclusion)

examples.en: A good conclusion was reached in the meeting.
An important result was obtained through the experiment.
An agreement will be reached as both sides talk.

examples.ko: 이 공식에서 답이 도출되는 과정을 설명해 주세요.
examples.en: Please explain how the answer is derived from this formula.

examples.ko: 조사 결과가 도출되기까지 한 달이 걸렸어요.
examples.en: It took a month before the survey results came out.
New ideas came out, and everyone was happy.

explain: 토론이나 연구에서 '결론이 도출되다', '합의가 도출되다'처럼 결과를 나타내는 명사와 짝을 이뤄요. 일상 대화에서는 '나오다'가 더 자연스러워요.
explain_en: In discussions and research it pairs with result nouns, as in 결론이 도출되다 and 합의가 도출되다. In daily talk 나오다 sounds more natural.

examples.en: The teacher urges students to read books.
The team leader finished the work while urging the staff on.
The city hall encouraged citizens to recycle.

examples.ko: 코치가 선수들을 큰 소리로 독려하고 있어요.
examples.en: The coach is urging the players on in a loud voice.
I prepared prizes to encourage the children to take part.
My parents urged me on, so I studied until the end.

explain: 그냥 응원하는 '격려하다'와 달리 윗사람이나 책임자가 일이나 공부를 더 열심히 하도록 이끄는 느낌이 있어요. 팀장·코치·기관이 쓸 때가 많고 '참여를 독려하다'처럼 자주 쓰는 짝말이 있어요.
explain_en: Unlike 격려하다, which is simple cheering, 독려하다 feels like a leader pushing people to work or study harder. Team leaders, coaches, and institutions use it often, with a common pairing like 참여를 독려하다.

en: bringing in; carrying in (to a restricted place)

examples.en: Bringing food into this building is prohibited.

examples.ko: 공연장에는 카메라 반입을 할 수 없어요.
examples.en: You cannot bring a camera into the concert hall.
Please check the list of items you may bring in.
Bringing liquids onto the plane is restricted.

examples.ko: 반입 검사 때문에 입구에서 줄을 섰어요.
examples.en: I lined up at the entrance for the bag check.

examples.ko: 외부 음료 반입 때문에 직원과 이야기했어요.
examples.en: I talked with the staff about bringing in outside drinks.

explain: 공항·공연장·학교처럼 규칙이 있는 곳에 물건을 들여올 때 써요. '반입 금지'가 가장 자주 보이는 짝이고 반대는 '반출'(밖으로 가지고 나감)이에요. 일상에서는 '가지고 들어오다'라고 해요.
explain_en: Use it for bringing things into places with rules, like airports, venues, and schools. 반입 금지 (no bringing in) is the most common pairing, and the opposite is 반출 (taking out). In daily talk people say 가지고 들어오다.

en: bring in; carry in (to a restricted place)

examples.en: You must not bring drinks into the library.

examples.ko: 공항에서 큰 가방을 반입할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: I could not bring the big bag in at the airport.
Please do not bring dangerous items in.
The guests brought in a cake and held a party.

examples.ko: 외부 음식을 반입하려면 미리 말해야 해요.
examples.en: If you want to bring in outside food, you have to say so in advance.

examples.ko: 그 나라는 과일을 반입하는 것을 검사해요.
examples.en: That country inspects the fruit people bring in.

explain: 허락이 필요하거나 검사를 받는 곳에 물건을 들일 때 써요. 규칙 문구에서 '반입하지 마세요'처럼 많이 보여요. 장 본 물건을 집에 들일 때는 쓰지 않아요.
explain_en: Use it for bringing things into places that need permission or inspection. It is common in rule notices, like 반입하지 마세요. You do not use it for bringing groceries home.

examples.en: This substance carries a cancer risk.

examples.ko: 발암 물질이 든 제품은 팔 수 없어요.
examples.en: Products containing carcinogens cannot be sold.
The research team is looking for the cause of cancer.

examples.ko: 뉴스에서 발암 가능성이 있는 식품을 소개했어요.
examples.en: The news introduced foods that may cause cancer.
There is an experiment that checks whether something causes cancer.

examples.ko: 탄 음식에는 발암 성분이 생길 수 있어요.
examples.en: Cancer-causing compounds can form in burnt food.

explain: '발암 물질', '발암 위험'처럼 뒤에 다른 명사가 붙는 합성어로 거의 쓰여요. 뉴스와 제품 안전 이야기에서 나와요. 혼자 쓸 때는 '암이 생기다'라고 풀어 말해요.
explain_en: It almost always works as the front of a compound, like 발암 물질 (carcinogen) and 발암 위험 (cancer risk). It appears in news and product safety talk. On its own, people spell it out as 암이 생기다.
